script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

TITLE: DO OVER

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

(40-something JOHN sits on the couch, staring at a photo album.
He's lost in thought, a mix of sadness and regret in his eyes.)

JOHN
(under his breath)
What if I could do it all over again?

Suddenly, JOHN's phone RINGS. He looks at the caller ID: MOM.

INT. JOHN'S BEDROOM - DAY

(JOHN answers the call.)

JOHN
Hi, Mom.

MOM
(tearful)
Johnny, I've got some news. Dad's been in a bad car accident. He's in the hospital, and the doctors say he might not make it.

John closes his eyes, and memories flood back.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - DAY (FLASHBACK)

(18-year-old JOHN watches as his father CRASHES through the gym window during a wrestling match. A tense silence follows, before the crowd erupts into laughter.)

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY (PRESENT)

(JOHN is visibly shaken, his thoughts consumed by his father's accident.)

JOHN
(to Mom)
I need to see him.

INT. HOSPITAL LOBBY - DAY

(JOHN enters the hospital, wiping away tears. He looks around, lost and uncertain.)

INT. HOSPITAL WAITING ROOM - DAY

(JOHN sits down across from his SISTER, LUCY. They share a moment of awkward silence.)

LUCY
(smiling)
Hey, John. It's good to see you.

JOHN
(sighs)
Yeah, you too, Lucy.

They sit in silence for a moment, both lost in their thoughts.

LUCY
(tearfully)
Dad's gonna pull through this, John. You know he will.

JOHN
(nods)
I know.

INT. HOSPITAL ROOM - NIGHT

(JOHN enters his father's hospital room. He approaches the bed, tears streaming down his face.)

FATHER
(weakly)
Johnny...

JOHN
(tearfully)
I'm here, Dad. I'm sorry for everything.

FATHER
(smiling weakly)
It's alright, son. You can't change the past, but you can make amends in the present.

INT. HOSPITAL CAFETERIA - DAY

(JOHN sits across from LUCY, a plate of food between them. They share a moment of understanding.)

LUCY
(smiling)
You know, John, maybe this is a chance for us all to start over.

JOHN
(nods)
You're right. And I'm going to make the most of it.

INT. JOHN'S APARTMENT - DAY (LATER)

(JOHN sits on the couch, surrounded by boxes. He's packing up his things, ready for a new start.)

INT. HOSPITAL LOBBY - DAY

(JOHN enters the lobby, looking determined. He spots an elderly woman, MRS. JENKINS, who's been sitting there since the accident. She looks up as he approaches.)

JOHN
(smiling)
Hello, Mrs. Jenkins. I couldn't help but notice you've been here since the accident.

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling back)
I was here for my husband. He passed away this morning.

They share a moment of silence.

JOHN
(softly)
I'm so sorry for your loss.

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling)
Thank you, dear. Sometimes, life gives us second chances. And sometimes, those second chances come when we least expect them.

JOHN
(nods)
I think you're right.

INT. HOSPITAL LOBBY - DAY (LATER)

(JOHN exits the hospital, his heart filled with newfound determination. He takes a deep breath, looking out at the world before him.)

FADE OUT.

End of screenplay.
